---
title: "Redefining Power Hitting"
subtitle: "How Jocelyn Alo and Oklahoma Broke Softball's Biggest Trade-Off (2021–2022)"
execute:
  echo: false
  message: false
  warning: false
---

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

batting_2021 <- read_csv("batting2021.csv") |> mutate(Season = 2021L)
batting_2022 <- read_csv("batting2022.csv") |> mutate(Season = 2022L)
all_batting <- bind_rows(batting_2021, batting_2022)
```

On the **Hitting Graphs** tab, striking out looks like plain bad news: players with more strikeouts generally end up with lower batting averages (meaning they get hits less often). However, batting average counts a soft single and a game-winning home run as the exact same thing. When we look at all 4,406 college softball player seasons from 2021 and 2022 and count **home runs** instead, we see the opposite pattern: players who hit the most home runs usually strike out *more* than average, because swinging hard for the fences comes with more swings and misses.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8.8
#| fig-height: 5.6
#| fig-dpi: 180
#| fig-alt: "Static scatter plot of Strikeouts vs. Home Runs across 4,406 NCAA D1 softball player-seasons in 2021 and 2022, colored by OPS, highlighting Jocelyn Alo, Tiare Jennings, Baylee Klingler, Addison Barnard, and Karli Spaid."

mean_k <- mean(all_batting$K)

featured <- all_batting |>
  filter(
    (Player == "Jocelyn Alo" & Season %in% c(2021L, 2022L)) |
      (Player == "Tiare Jennings" & Season == 2022L) |
      (Player == "Baylee Klingler" & Season == 2022L) |
      (Player == "Addison Barnard" & Season == 2022L) |
      (Player == "Karli Spaid" & Season == 2022L)
  )

all_batting |>
  ggplot(aes(x = K, y = HR, color = OPS)) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = mean_k,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "gray50",
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.45, size = 1.8) +
  geom_smooth(
    aes(group = 1),
    method = "lm",
    se = FALSE,
    color = "#b91c1c",
    linewidth = 0.9
  ) +
  geom_point(
    data = featured,
    shape = 21,
    size = 3.8,
    stroke = 1.2,
    color = "#111827",
    aes(fill = OPS),
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(option = "magma", direction = -1, name = "OPS") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(option = "magma", direction = -1) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = mean_k + 0.9,
    y = 28.5,
    label = "College Avg: 21 Strikeouts",
    hjust = 0,
    size = 3.2,
    color = "gray35",
    fontface = "italic"
  ) +
  annotate(
    "label",
    x = 14.5,
    y = 37.0,
    label = "Jocelyn Alo (Oklahoma '21 & '22)\n34 HRs each year · only 16 & 19 strikeouts",
    size = 3.1,
    fontface = "bold",
    fill = "#fef2f2",
    color = "#7f1d1d",
    label.size = 0.35
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 11.6,
    y = 30.0,
    label = "Tiare Jennings ('22)\n29 HRs, 13 strikeouts",
    hjust = 1,
    size = 3.0,
    fontface = "bold",
    color = "#1f2937"
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 7.6,
    y = 24.0,
    label = "Baylee Klingler ('22)\n24 HRs, 6 strikeouts",
    hjust = 0,
    size = 3.0,
    fontface = "bold",
    color = "#1f2937"
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 38.5,
    y = 33.2,
    label = "Addison Barnard ('22)\n33 HRs, 37 strikeouts",
    hjust = 0,
    size = 3.0,
    fontface = "bold",
    color = "#1f2937"
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 40.5,
    y = 27.8,
    label = "Karli Spaid ('22)\n28 HRs, 39 strikeouts",
    hjust = 0,
    size = 3.0,
    fontface = "bold",
    color = "#1f2937"
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 68), breaks = seq(0, 60, by = 10)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 39.5), breaks = seq(0, 35, by = 5)) +
  labs(
    title = "Power Usually Costs Strikeouts — Except at the Very Top",
    subtitle = "NCAA Division I Softball (2021–2022, 4,406 player seasons)",
    x = "Strikeouts (K)",
    y = "Home Runs (HR)",
    caption = "Source: NCAA Division I Softball Batting Statistics (2021 & 2022). Darker points indicate higher overall hitting production (OPS)."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = "gray35", size = 11),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```

In the chart above, each dot is a player's season, and darker purple dots mark stronger overall hitters (measured by `OPS`, a single rating that combines how often a batter reaches base and how far they hit the ball). For most big sluggers, power comes with a clear trade-off. To the right of the dashed average line (21 strikeouts), stars like Wichita State's Addison Barnard (33 home runs, 37 strikeouts) and Miami (OH)'s Karli Spaid (28 home runs, 39 strikeouts) struck out nearly twice as often as a typical player, yet more than made up for those outs by driving the ball over the fence.

Then there is Oklahoma's **Jocelyn Alo**, sitting at the very top left of the chart, who ignored that trade-off completely. In *both* 2021 and 2022, Alo led the entire country with **34 home runs** while striking out just **16 and 19 times**—fewer strikeouts than an average college player who hit fewer than four home runs all season. By 2022, opposing pitchers were so afraid to throw strikes to her that she walked 54 times and still got a hit in more than half of her official at-bats, breaking the all-time college career home run record (122 homers). Alongside teammate Tiare Jennings—who also crushed 29 home runs with only 13 strikeouts in 2022—Alo helped make Oklahoma nearly impossible to pitch to, powering the Sooners to back-to-back national championships.

**Putting Oklahoma's Run in Perspective (2021–2022)**  
Over these two seasons, a typical Division I softball hitter averaged about **4 home runs** and **21 strikeouts** per year. Oklahoma teammates Jocelyn Alo and Tiare Jennings combined for **124 home runs** while striking out only **65 times total** across both years—giving the Sooners historic power without giving away easy outs on their way to two straight Women's College World Series titles.
:::
